questions: Did these movements begin or worsen after zonisamide was stopped?
Did they improve after zonisamide was restarted?
Do your arms suddenly lose strength or drop while you are holding them out?
Do the movements consist of brief, shock-like jerks?
Do they occur when you are maintaining a posture or using your hands?
Do they disappear completely during sleep?
Do you feel an urge or unpleasant sensation before making the movement?
Do the movements lessen when you are distracted?
Are the movements present when you are relaxed and not using your arms?
Have you ever lost awareness during these episodes?
Have you ever fallen or injured yourself because of them?
Do you have tongue biting, urinary incontinence, or confusion after an episode?
Do you have weakness, numbness, speech difficulty, or visual symptoms during or after the movements?
Have you had similar movements in your face, neck, trunk, or legs?
Have you previously been diagnosed with epilepsy or another seizure disorder?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed any other medication?
results: 1. cognitive screen (MMSE / MoCA / FAB): MMSE 23/30 and Frontal Assessment Battery 9/18 - frontal/executive dysfunction
2. copper / caeruloplasmin / 24 h urinary copper: normal - excludes Wilson disease
3. genetic testing (targeted panel or exome): NOTCH2NLC GGC repeat expansion - genetically confirmed NIID
4. skin biopsy: eosinophilic, p62- and ubiquitin-POSITIVE intranuclear inclusions in adipocytes, sweat gland cells and fibroblasts - diagnostic of NIID
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID) caused by a pathogenic NOTCH2NLC GGC-repeat expansion, with associated frontal/executive dysfunction and postural tremor.

Alternative: Fragile X–associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (FMR1 premutation)

Alternative: Essential tremor

Alternative: Parkinsonian or other neurodegenerative tremor syndrome
dx: Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID) caused by a pathogenic NOTCH2NLC GGC-repeat expansion, with associated frontal/executive dysfunction and postural tremor.
